title: Exact Nagaoka-to-spiral transition in the doped infinite-U triangular lattice
abstract: We study the single-hole infinite-$U$ Hubbard model on the triangular lattice with nearest- and next-nearest-neighbor hoppings $t_1$ and $t_2$. A frustrating $t_2$ destabilizes Nagaoka ferromagnetism through a Lifshitz transition to a long-wavelength coplanar spiral at $t_{2,c}/t_1=-0.182$. We determine the critical point analytically by reducing the many-body problem to an effective two-body hole--magnon scattering problem in which the hard-core hole--magnon constraint is treated exactly. Numerical calculations confirm the spiral ground state and reveal a coherent spin polaron with quasiparticle weight $Z\simeq0.92$ at the Lifshitz-shifted momentum $\mathbf{K}=-\mathbf{Q}^*$. These results establish the first quantum instability of the triangular-lattice Nagaoka ferromagnet and provide the magnetic baseline for magnon-mediated pairing at finite doping.
summary: This work precisely locates the quantum critical point where Nagaoka ferromagnetism destabilizes into an incommensurate spiral state on a triangular lattice. By combining analytical theory with advanced numerical methods, the authors establish $t_{2,c}/t_1 = -0.182$ as the transition boundary. This provides crucial theoretical insight into magnetic fluctuations and pairing mechanisms in doped correlated electron systems.
main_problem: The study determines the exact quantum instability point where Nagaoka ferromagnetism breaks down into a long-wavelength coplanar spiral state in a doped triangular lattice.
main_result: The transition occurs at a critical hopping ratio of $t_{2,c}/t_1 = -0.182$, establishing the first quantum instability of this ferromagnetic phase and providing a baseline for magnon-mediated pairing.
method: The problem is solved by reducing it to an effective two-body hole–magnon scattering problem, utilizing analytical calculations combined with rigorous numerical techniques like Exact Diagonalization (ED) and spectral flow analysis.
model_or_system: The system is the single-hole infinite-$U$ Hubbard model on a triangular lattice, incorporating nearest-neighbor ($t_1$) and next-nearest-neighbor ($t_2$) hopping terms. The physics is governed by kinetic energy minimization in the presence of strong correlations.
key_observables: Spiral stiffness coefficient ($c_2$), quasiparticle weight ($Z \simeq 0.92$), ground-state energy difference $E(\Phi) - E_{FM}$ vs. magnetic flux $\Phi$, and the optimal spiral wavevector $Q^*$.
important_parameters: The critical hopping ratio $t_{2,c}/t_1 = -0.182$ is central; the model operates in the infinite-$U$ limit.
main_assumptions: The analysis treats the hard-core hole–magnon constraint exactly and relies on small-$Q$ expansions near criticality to characterize the continuous nature of the transition.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the vanishing spiral stiffness at $t_{2,c}/t_1 = -0.182$, show the formation of an energy minimum (spiral well) in spectral flow plots as $|t_2|$ increases, and map out polaron dispersion curves in the resulting spiral phase.
paper_structure: The paper systematically analyzes the instability by first deriving effective Hamiltonians, then using analytical methods to pinpoint the critical point ($t_{2,c}/t_1 = -0.182$), confirming this result with ED and spectral flow analysis across multiple diagnostics (e.g., energy vs. flux, quasiparticle weight).
why_interesting: The rigorous determination of a quantum phase transition boundary in a highly correlated model like the Hubbard model is fundamental to understanding magnetic ordering mechanisms relevant to high-temperature superconductivity.
